newsitem.title: LEBANON: Arab summit may be held soon, Meguid says.
newsitem.headline: Arab summit may be held soon, Meguid says.

text.p: An Arab summit may be held soon to discuss measures to counter Israel's plans to build a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, Arab League Secretary-General Esmat Abdel-Meguid said on Thursday.

"I imagine that contacts between Arab leaders at present may lead to invitations to an Arab summit, even if a mini-summit," Meguid told reporters at Beirut airport in response to a question on Arab plans to counter the Israeli decision.
Meguid said Israel's decision last month to build 6,500 houses for Jews in Jabal Abu Ghneim or Har Homa "threatens the peace process in the region".
Israel says all of Jerusalem is its capital. Palestinians want East Jerusalem, which Israel seized during the 1967 Middle East War, to be the capital of a future Palestinian state.

Meguid is visiting Lebanon to deliver a speech on Friday at a rally marking the 19th anniversary of Israel's first invasion of the country. The Jewish state holds a border buffer zone in south Lebanon to prevent guerrilla raids on northern Israel.
